title: The set must account for its exit
technology: temporary production, sorting, packaging and carbon documentation
governingQuestion: What changes when teardown is designed before the first look appears?
status: evidence-backed production draft; recording, interviews, specialist review and owner-final approval remain open

longform.headline: The set must account for its exit
longform.opening: In Copenhagen, the set is asked to account for what happens after it disappears.

sections.heading: Then
sections.copy: Current CPHFW terms require show-production measures including waste sorting, avoidance of single-use backstage plastic and zero-waste set design under the framework’s stated definition.

sections.heading: Now
sections.copy: The terms permit a CPHFW representative to review backstage compliance on show day and allow additional documentation within a month; this is an operational evidence path, not an independent environmental audit.

sections.heading: Next—and the limit
sections.copy: Show-level material inventories, energy use, transport boundaries, carbon calculations, suppliers and teardown outcomes remain unavailable unless brands or producers release them.

longform.closing: Copenhagen’s distinction is not a claim of purity. It is the decision to make participation depend on evidence—and the obligation to keep asking what that evidence cannot establish.
